categories.narrative: Recommendation, situation, argument, decision and findings
categories.comparison_evidence: Comparisons, alternatives, evidence, requirements and response
categories.approach_delivery: Approaches, phases, activities, deliverables and execution method
categories.roadmap: Time, milestones, releases and workstream sequencing
categories.team_credentials: Responsibilities, pods, roster, biography and experience
categories.outcomes_commercial: Benefits, measures, commercial options, scope and value
categories.visual_storytelling: Photography, quotations, proof stories and visual explanations
categories.business_architecture: Business capabilities, value streams, operating models and organizational domains
categories.technical_architecture: System context, applications, data, integration, platform and deployment views
categories.product_overview: Portfolio, product proposition, audience, outcomes and top-level capabilities
categories.product_detail: Capability mechanics, feature detail, workflow, interfaces and product evidence
categories.layers_components: Layered models, decomposition, building blocks and component relationships
categories.framing_navigation: Section framing, agenda, context, scope and overview-to-detail navigation
categories.reference_instruction: Brand instructions, source-only references and unsuitable authoring examples

altitudes.framing: Establish why, the decision, scope or how to read the following section.
altitudes.overview: Show the whole and its major parts without fully explaining each part.
altitudes.explanation: Explain relationships, choices or how something works.
altitudes.detail: Describe one bounded part with mechanisms, responsibilities, evidence or specifications.
altitudes.reference: Provide lookup material, exhaustive records or instructions.

densities.sparse: Substantial whitespace and a small number of content units.
densities.medium: Moderate supporting detail across a few zones.
densities.dense: Document-style detail across many units or substantial prose.

rules: Altitude and density are independent. A dense overview is valid.
Category is the source occurrence’s primary use; families retain all observed categories.
Color changes, copy changes and repeated occurrences do not create a new template family.
Different slot structures or supported behavior may justify separate arrangements.
Multi-slide sequences are separate catalog items and never inflate template counts.
Architecture and product views are included even where advanced automatic routing remains unsupported.
All capacities are unmeasured until native evidence qualifies a contract.
